meta.title: Completion suggestions are offered when typing "." in comment on first line
meta.fix_ref: 0bbf5db8a1 (Fixed bug that caused completion suggestions to be presented when typing a period within a comment on the first line of the file), 2020-11-07; first in 1.1.84 (maintainer: 'addressed in Pyright 1.1.84')
meta.build_notes: npm pyright@1.1.83 (2020-11-04) and pyright@1.1.84 (2020-11-08); the fix commit is the only completion change between the two tags.
meta.notes: Not reproduced (1 attempt): pre-fix 1.1.83 answered an empty completion list for the '.' at the end of the first-line comment, in the original and in the shifted copy. Reading the pre-fix code (completionProvider._isWithinComment: tokens.getItemAtPosition(offset) < 0 -> 'not in a comment') suggests the defect concerns comments that precede the file's first token, which a one-line comment-only file does not have, and which a blank line inserted above would not change; the R5 relation with a blank line therefore cannot separate the builds, and no probe asserts that a completion list is empty. Not retried: a second attempt would need invented code after the comment and a transformation chosen from the fix.

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the session defaults apply.

files.source: issue body (prose only: 'a comment is created on the first line of a source file, typing "." within that comment')
files.note: the issue has no code; a one-line file whose first line is a comment ending in the typed '.'

repro.steps: Open main.py, whose first line is a comment, and request completions right after the '.' typed in it (line 1, character 10). Reported: completion suggestions appear inside the comment on the first line; they should never appear within a comment. Probe (R5): a copy with a blank line inserted above the comment must give the same completion answer at the mapped position (the report is specific to the first line).
